title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming & response formatting
author: Marisa Chen
description: Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions to parity with OpenAI semantics for params, roles and stop/logprobs handling; stabilize streaming output for tool/function-calling workflows; and fix response formatting differences observed in downstream clients. This PR implements parameter normalization (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, presence/ frequency penalties), role mapping semantics (system/user/assistant/content handling), stop sequences and logprobs output compatibility, and a more robust streaming protocol for function/tool calls. Summary of changes: - Normalize incoming OpenAI-style params into internal serving config with explicit precedence and validation. - Implement exact stop-sequence trimming behavior and deterministic logprobs shape for token-level outputs. - Stabilize streaming boundary conditions for partial tokens and function-call event frames; add backpressure handling so client-facing streams don't interleave JSON control frames with token frames. - Add response-formatting layer that produces the same message/choices structure (delta events, finish_reason, index ordering). - Extend SDK shims (Python) and examples to demonstrate new behavior. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged for existing Redwood API usage; OpenAI compatibility toggle enables this path. Checklist: [x] param mapping implemented [x] stop/logprobs shape tests added [x] streaming function-call frames stabilized [x] SDK and docs updated [x] integration tests covering hybrid workflows
commits: Commit summary: 1) normalize-params: add param normalizer with precedence rules and validation (Marisa) 2) stop-logprobs: implement stop trimming and canonical logprobs shape (Sofia) 3) streaming-fix: introduce stream frame types and backpressure logic (Ethan) 4) sdk-shim: python compatibility updates and examples (Rahul) 5) tests: unit and integration coverage for parity cases 6) docs: openai_compat.md and changelog entry

release_notes: Adds OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility mode: param normalization (temp/top_p/max_tokens/penalties), role semantics alignment, deterministic stop-sequence trimming, canonical logprobs output, and more stable streaming for function/tool-calling workflows. SDK examples updated.
